title: Elizabeth's Reception at Netherfield Dinner and Caroline's Criticism of Jane's Manners
summary: Elizabeth finds few allies at dinner, with only Caroline's brother showing her kindness. After she leaves, Caroline and Louisa harshly criticize Jane's appearance, clothing, and manners.

title: Section 4: Story So Far Recap and Picture Observation Activity
summary: A review box summarizes events up to Elizabeth meeting Mr Wickham at a dinner party, followed by a prompt asking why Elizabeth looks shocked in the picture and exercises to complete.

title: Mr Wickham Explains How He Was Cheated Out of His Late Godfather's Inheritance
summary: Wickham tells Elizabeth that Mr Darcy's late father intended to provide for him, but the inheritance was given to someone else instead, claiming Wickham had squandered it.

title: Section 5: Story So Far Recap and Picture Observation Activity
summary: A review box summarizes events from the Netherfield ball and Mr Collins' proposals through Elizabeth's trip to the countryside, where Fitzwilliam hints that Darcy separated a friend from the wrong person.

title: Elizabeth Confronts Darcy Over Bingley and Jane and Accuses Him of Ruining Wickham
summary: Elizabeth angrily accuses Darcy of separating Bingley from Jane and of reducing Wickham to poverty by withholding his rightful inheritance, while Darcy reacts with irritation.

title: Section 6: Story So Far Recap and Picture Observation Activity
summary: A review box summarizes events from Darcy's letter and Elizabeth's visit to Pemberley through Lydia's elopement with Wickham, followed by a prompt to guess what Elizabeth and Darcy are discussing.

title: Darcy Repeats His Proposal to Elizabeth and She Accepts Him Joyfully
summary: Darcy asks Elizabeth whether her feelings have changed since April; she responds with gratitude and pleasure, and they share a warm conversation about their newfound understanding.

title: As You Like It: Match Texts About Shakespeare's Life, His Plays, and the Play's Importance
summary: An exercise asking students to match three headings — about Shakespeare's biography, the story, and the importance of the play — with the corresponding descriptive texts.
